short: An Athenian philosopher who founded the Academy and wrote foundational dialogues exploring justice, reality, and the soul.
full:
A devoted student of Socrates, Plato authored dozens of philosophical dialogues that remain central to the Western intellectual tradition. In his most famous work, the Republic, he outlined a utopian society ruled by philosopher-kings and introduced the Theory of Forms, which argued that the physical world is only a shadow of a higher, perfect reality.

Plato established the Academy in Athens, widely considered the first institution of higher learning in the Western world. His comprehensive philosophical system influenced centuries of later thought, deeply shaping both classical philosophy and the eventual development of Christian theology.
